methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses paired peripheral and tumor 5' single-cell RNA + TCR + CITE-seq on 9 NSCLC surgical patients to define circulating tumor-reactive T cells (cTR-T) via TCR clonal matching to tumor-infiltrating TR-T (defined by MANAscore UCell algorithm with a modified threshold). Validation includes a 70-patient ICI-treated metastatic NSCLC cohort with reference UMAP projection, MART1-specific melanoma TCR clone enrichment, and a BPmel-1-SIY engineered melanoma mouse model with anti-PD-L1 therapy (n=14 total, n=10 per group, randomized). Statistical rigor is strengthened by a novel Consistency score across samples to retain genes with directionally concordant fold-change in >=2/3 of samples, use of Mann-Whitney-based UCell for robustness to dropout, and Harmony batch correction. Limitations: the discovery cohort is small (n=9), the TR-T definition depends on MANAscore thresholds applied heuristically, and ICI cohort response labels are not detailed in the excerpt.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design combines a small prospective surgical cohort and a 70-patient metastatic NSCLC ICI cohort for biomarker validation, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b (individual cohort study). Clinical relevance is high: a blood-based biomarker (pre-treatment CD38-low cTR-Ts; post-dose TCF7+ stem-like transition) that predicts ICI response would be directly actionable given the noninvasive sampling, and CD49a/CD49b/HLA-DR surface markers enable flow-based translation.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the closest fit for this prognostic biomarker study (TR-T phenotype predicting ICI response). IRB approval at Kyoto University (G1012) and animal committee approval are stated. Both sexes included. Sample-collection SOPs (14 mL EDTA, LeucoSep, CELLBANKER cryopreservation), cell sorting gates (CD45+CD8+), antibody clones/dilutions, Cell Ranger v7.0.1, Seurat v4, Harmony v1.2.0, Monocle3 v1.3.1, and DSB v1.0.3 are explicitly reported. Humane endpoints defined (>20% body weight loss, 1000 mm^3 tumor volume). Randomization of mice into groups is stated. Data-deposition accession numbers are not stated in the provided excerpt.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper addresses a long-standing gap: phenotyping of circulating tumor-reactive T cells in ICI-treated NSCLC, which has been limited by cTR-T rarity (<0.1%) and lack of markers. Using TCR as a clonal barcode between paired TILs and PBMCs to identify cTR-Ts without relying on known antigens (MART1-style approaches) is methodologically novel. The identification of CD49a/CD49b/HLA-DR as cTR-T surface markers and the transition to TCF7+ stem-like phenotype post-ICI in responders are new observations. Prior work on clonal replacement (Yost/Wu) and peripheral biomarkers is acknowledged; this extends them with TCR-anchored reactivity.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear rationale, rigorous methods, and a formal Consistency-score equation described with LaTeX formatting (cosmetic artifacts from corpus normalization). Methods are thorough and reproducible; the flow cytometry panels are exhaustively detailed. Some duplication (antibody lists repeated in blocks) appears to be an artifact of the markdown conversion.

key_strengths: Paired scRNA+TCR+CITE-seq on 9 NSCLC patients enables antigen-agnostic identification of cTR-Ts by TCR clonal barcoding against tumor-resident TR-Ts
Identification of CD49a, CD49b, and HLA-DR as surface markers of cTR-Ts, with progenitor-like phenotype from Monocle3 trajectory analysis
Validation cohort of 70 ICI-treated metastatic NSCLC patients linking pre-treatment CD38-low and post-dose TCF7+ cTR-Ts to response
Mechanistic cross-validation in BPmel-1-SIY mouse melanoma model with anti-PD-L1 and SIY-tetramer phenotyping
key_concerns: Discovery cohort is small (n=9 NSCLC surgical patients); MANAscore cutoffs were modified ad hoc to accommodate cell-number imbalance
Response definitions and patient characteristics for the 70-patient ICI cohort are not fully described in the methods excerpt
Data-deposition accession numbers for single-cell data are not clearly reported in the available text
The Consistency score is a study-specific heuristic; its operating characteristics should be benchmarked against standard meta-analytic approaches
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically innovative peripheral-blood biomarker study in NSCLC ICI with strong multi-model support; top-tier plausible (Nature Medicine / Nature Cancer) with minor revisions on cohort description and data deposition.
